step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified actors and AWS services from whiteboard icons: Engineers (actor icon), UI (web console icon), S3, Elemental MediaConvert, SageMaker, Lambda (two separate instances), and DynamoDB.
2. Filtered out handwritten floating text ('10,000s', '22% -> 7%', '66 -> 7', '65,000', '400,000').
3. Traced explicit arrows to build edges:
   - Engineers -> UI
   - UI -> S3
   - UI -> Elemental MediaConvert
   - Elemental MediaConvert -> lower Lambda
   - SageMaker -> lower Lambda
   - lower Lambda -> DynamoDB
   - DynamoDB <-> upper Lambda (bidirectional arrow).

graph.name: Levin Automated Road Inspection Architecture
graph.notes: Automated road inspection system processing tens of thousands of video frames in parallel using AWS serverless and machine learning services.

nodes.name: Engineers
nodes.notes: Field engineers who record and upload road inspection video footage.

nodes.name: UI
nodes.notes: Web interface where engineers upload video and review detected defects.

nodes.name: Elemental MediaConvert
nodes.notes: Splits uploaded video into individual image frames.

nodes.name: SageMaker
nodes.notes: Trained ML model for detecting road defects.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Executes ML inference on individual video frames.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores defect metadata and frame analytical results.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Processes and deduplicates metadata stored in DynamoDB.

edges.notes: Engineers upload inspection video via the web UI.
Raw video is stored in S3.
Video sent to MediaConvert for frame splitting.
Extracted frames trigger parallel Lambda execution.
SageMaker model packaged inside Lambda function.
Inference Lambda writes detection metadata to DynamoDB.
DynamoDB sends metadata to deduplication Lambda.
Deduplication Lambda writes merged defects back to DynamoDB.
